title: Air India Launches Maharaja Shop, Turning Loyalty Points Into Everyday Shopping
excerpt: The members-only marketplace lets Maharaja Club members earn points on electronics, luggage, jewellery and exclusive Air India merchandise, redeemable for award flights and upgrades.
body:
• Air India has launched The Maharaja Shop, a members-only online marketplace where Maharaja Club members earn Maharaja Points on everyday lifestyle purchases.
  • Categories include electronics, luggage, travel accessories, fragrances, home essentials, wellness products, watches and jewellery, plus an exclusive Air India merchandise collection available nowhere else.
  • Points earned can be redeemed for Award Flights and Cabin Upgrades on Air India; members can also redeem on Air India Express and 25 Star Alliance partner airlines.
  • What it means for you: if you collect Maharaja Points for US-India trips, everyday shopping at The Maharaja Shop now builds your balance without flying — earning rates vary by product, reported at Rs 30 to Rs 134 of spend per point.

Air India has launched The Maharaja Shop, a lifestyle marketplace exclusively for members of its frequent flyer programme, Maharaja Club, the airline announced on November 5. The platform lets members earn Maharaja Points on eligible purchases from Indian and international brands, extending the programme beyond flights for the first time into a dedicated retail channel of its own.

How it works

Members shop through themaharajashop.com across categories including electronics, luggage, travel accessories, fragrances, home essentials, wellness products, watches and jewellery, according to Air India's announcement. Complimentary shipping is available on eligible orders. The points collected can be redeemed towards Award Flights and Cabin Upgrades on Air India.

There is no single earning rate. Live From A Lounge, which reviewed the live store, reported that the rate varies by product, at Rs 30 to Rs 134 per one Maharaja Club point, with each product showing its own points figure. That spread matters: at the generous end, shopping here builds a balance quickly; at the other, it is a modest top-up. Air India has not published a fixed rate card for the shop.

"Maharaja Club is evolving into a comprehensive lifestyle loyalty programme that rewards members well beyond their travel journeys."

— Sunil Suresh, Head of Loyalty, E-Commerce and Marketing, Air India

The exclusive merchandise draw

The most distinctive part of the launch is a collection of Air India-branded merchandise available only through the shop. It includes Maharaja magnets and collectibles, aircraft-inspired keychains, lapel pins, postcard sets, coaster sets and travel essentials, the airline said. For collectors and frequent flyers in the diaspora — readers who grew up with the Maharaja mascot on family trips to India — that range is the part of the store with no equivalent elsewhere.

The shop itself is operated by Vernost, the travel and loyalty solutions company that also runs Axis Bank's TravelEDGE programme, Live From A Lounge reported.

Where it fits in Maharaja Club

Maharaja Club members already earn points through Air India, Air India Express and more than 100 partners across airlines, hospitality, retail, lifestyle and financial services, and can redeem on Air India, Air India Express and 25 Star Alliance partner airlines, with tier privileges covering more than 1,100 airport lounges worldwide. Air India has been expanding that partner network steadily — its Maharaja Club newsroom announcements mark the programme passing 100 partnerships. The Maharaja Shop is different in kind, though: it is Air India's own storefront, not a partner link-out.

Access is members-only. Travellers who are not enrolled can register for Maharaja Club and then begin earning points on purchases through the marketplace, the airline said. For diaspora readers, the practical test will be the delivered price and earn rate on each item against ordinary retailers — the points are a bonus on a purchase you would make anyway, not yet a reason on their own to pay over the odds.
